title: D003: Implement infrastructure deployment automation E2E
summary: Implements `make deploy-infra`, `make teardown-infra`, `make install-test-deps`, and `make e2e` targets with orchestration scripts, kustomize overlays for kind-specific sizing, a Chainsaw E2E test covering all 12 infrastructure health assertions, and a GitHub Actions `e2e-infra` CI job. Overall implementation is well-structured and follows project conventions. One blocking issue: init-unseal.sh hardcodes a 3-replica PODS array that will fail on the standalone (1-replica) kind deployment because openbao-1 and openbao-2 do not exist. One major inconsistency: the wait_for_externalsecrets function and the Chainsaw test check different ExternalSecret condition types.

tests_checklist.item: Test covers ClusterIssuer, MariaDB CR, Memcached CR Ready conditions
Test uses extended 5m assert timeout for operator startup
Full deploy-infra + e2e + teardown-infra cycle works end-to-end

code_quality_checklist.item: Shell scripts follow project conventions (SPDX header, set -euo pipefail, CC-0010 reference, log() with timestamps)
CI job follows existing conventions (SHA-pinned actions, permissions, concurrency, runs-on)
Kustomize overlays do not modify production manifests
Scripts are idempotent (preflight checks, existing cluster detection)
Helper functions are well-documented with comments
No dead code or unused variables

security_checklist.item: No hardcoded secrets in scripts or configs
BAO_TOKEN extracted from K8s Secret, not hardcoded
CI actions are SHA-pinned to prevent supply-chain attacks
No shell injection in sh -c commands

architecture_checklist.item: Two-phase kustomization pattern followed (base for operators, infrastructure for CRD-dependent resources)
Kind overlays patch production manifests via kustomize, not modify them
OpenBao bootstrap scripts invoked as-is without modification
Solution is as simple as possible for the requirements
CI job independent of lint/test jobs (no needs: dependency)

dry_yagni_checklist.item: Shared log() pattern consistent across all scripts

fail_fast_checklist.item: Pre-flight checks detect Docker not running

defensive_checklist.item: Existing cluster detected and handled gracefully
Teardown idempotent (exits 0 if cluster doesn't exist)
install-test-deps skips download if correct version exists
Environment variable defaults provided for all configurable values

security_findings.description: install-test-deps.sh downloads binaries from GitHub releases and dl.k8s.io without verifying checksums or signatures. A compromised CDN or MITM attack could serve malicious binaries. While HTTPS mitigates transport-level attacks, checksum verification provides defense-in-depth.
security_findings.fix: Add SHA-256 checksum verification after download for each tool. Store expected checksums as constants at the top of the script (alongside version pins). Verify with: echo "${EXPECTED_HASH} ${INSTALL_DIR}/${name}" | sha256sum -c -

architecture_findings.description: FC4: deploy-infra.sh calls init-unseal.sh without overriding the PODS variable. init-unseal.sh (CC-0009) hardcodes PODS=("openbao-0" "openbao-1" "openbao-2") at line 22 as a direct assignment (not env-overridable). In standalone mode (1 replica deployed by the kind overlay), pods openbao-1 and openbao-2 do not exist. The unseal_pod function will fail with 'ERROR: Could not reach openbao-1' and exit 1, aborting the entire deployment at step 7. The review criteria explicitly expected 'PODS variable override for standalone mode' in deploy-infra.sh, but no override mechanism exists.
architecture_findings.fix: Two changes needed: (1) In deploy/openbao/bootstrap/init-unseal.sh, make PODS env-overridable by changing line 22 from `PODS=("openbao-0" "openbao-1" "openbao-2")` to `if [[ -z "${OPENBAO_PODS:-}" ]]; then PODS=("openbao-0" "openbao-1" "openbao-2"); else IFS=',' read -ra PODS <<< "${OPENBAO_PODS}"; fi`. (2) In hack/deploy-infra.sh, before calling init-unseal.sh at line 201, add: `export OPENBAO_PODS="openbao-0"` to restrict unseal to the single standalone replica.

issues_found.description: init-unseal.sh PODS hardcoded for 3 replicas — will fail on standalone kind cluster. deploy-infra.sh calls init-unseal.sh without any mechanism to override the PODS array. unseal_pod() will exit 1 when kubectl exec fails for non-existent openbao-1.
issues_found.fix: Make PODS env-overridable in init-unseal.sh and export OPENBAO_PODS=openbao-0 from deploy-infra.sh before calling init-unseal.sh.

issues_found.description: ExternalSecret condition type mismatch: wait_for_externalsecrets() checks `.type == "Ready"` but chainsaw-test.yaml checks `.type == "SecretSynced"`. If the ESO version uses only one of these condition types, one check will fail while the other passes. Both should use the same condition type for consistency.
issues_found.fix: Align both to use the same condition type. ESO v0.10+ uses `Ready` as the primary status condition. Change chainsaw-test.yaml assertions from `type == 'SecretSynced'` to `type == 'Ready'`, OR change the jq filter in wait_for_externalsecrets to check `SecretSynced` instead of `Ready`. The latter is preferred if `SecretSynced` is the more specific/accurate condition for the ESO version deployed.

issues_found.description: SCRIPT_DIR is declared but never used. Dead variable.

suggested_improvements: Add SHA-256 checksum verification to install-test-deps.sh for downloaded binaries (defense-in-depth against supply-chain attacks)
Add a preflight check in deploy-infra.sh for required CLI tools (flux, kind, kubectl, jq) before starting deployment, providing a clear error message listing missing tools
Consider adding a `--report-file` flag to the CI chainsaw invocation to ensure JUnit output lands in _output/reports/ even if the global chainsaw-config.yaml report path changes
next_steps: Fix BLOCKING: Make init-unseal.sh PODS variable env-overridable and add OPENBAO_PODS=openbao-0 export in deploy-infra.sh before bootstrap invocation
Fix MAJOR: Align ExternalSecret condition type between wait_for_externalsecrets() and chainsaw-test.yaml
Fix MINOR: Remove unused SCRIPT_DIR from teardown-infra.sh

detected_patterns.name: Environment-variable-configurable timeouts with trailing-s strip for arithmetic
detected_patterns.applies_when: Writing a shell script wait function that accepts a human-readable timeout string (e.g., '600s') from an environment variable and needs to use it in both kubectl --timeout and bash arithmetic comparisons
detected_patterns.description: Wait helper functions accept a timeout string with trailing 's' suffix (e.g., '600s') from environment variables, strip the suffix for arithmetic comparisons (`timeout_secs="${timeout%s}"`), and use the original value for kubectl --timeout which accepts the 's' suffix natively. This avoids maintaining two separate timeout variables and follows the convention established by kubectl's timeout format.

  # Strip trailing 's' for arithmetic if present.

detected_patterns.name: Two-phase kind kustomize overlay referencing production base
detected_patterns.applies_when: Adding kind-specific resource sizing or configuration that differs from production manifests in deploy/flux-system/
detected_patterns.description: Kind-specific differences are expressed as kustomize overlays in deploy/kind/ that reference the production manifests via relative paths (../../flux-system/ for base, ../../flux-system/infrastructure/ for CRD-dependent resources). The overlays use strategic merge patches to adjust replicas, storage classes, and HA settings without modifying the production manifests. This mirrors the two-phase kustomization pattern from deploy/flux-system/ (base for operators, infrastructure for CRD-dependent resources) and ensures kind testing validates the same manifests that ship to production with only resource sizing differences.
